- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days), suggesting a persistent upward bias.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop sharply, indicating an overshoot after spikes — correct by smoothing out the peak and reducing the immediate drop.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the forecast horizon (last 10–15 days), suggesting a mean-reversion bias — adjust downward gradually toward the historical mean.
- Forecasts often lag behind true outcomes by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle of the forecast window — consider adding a 1–2 day lag correction or using rolling window smoothing.
- When true prices spike (e.g., >80), model tends to overreact and forecast even higher — reduce forecast sensitivity to sudden spikes.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in the final 5–7 days — add a decay factor or trend filter to dampen late-period overconfidence.
